biography:
Crash Test Dummies are a Canadian rock band from Winnipeg, Manitoba, formed in the late 1980s around singer-songwriter Brad Roberts, whose unusually deep bass-baritone voice became the group’s signature sound. The best-known lineup also included Ellen Reid, Dan Roberts, Benjamin Darvill, and Mitch Dorge, and the band’s literate, wry approach drew on folk, pop, alternative rock, and occasional Celtic and country touches. Their roots can be traced to Winnipeg’s club scene, where Roberts and Curtis Riddell had played in earlier, looser projects before the band took shape under the name Crash Test Dummies.

The group broke through in Canada with “Superman’s Song” in 1991 and achieved international fame with their 1993 album God Shuffled His Feet, led by the hit single “Mmm Mmm Mmm Mmm.” That record’s unusual blend of catchy melodies, dry humor, and eccentric lyrics made them one of the most distinctive alternative rock acts of the 1990s. Crash Test Dummies became known for turning thoughtful, often quirky storytelling into mainstream rock songs, and their sound and voice helped set them apart from their peers while earning them a lasting place in 90s rock and pop history.
name: Crash Test Dummies
